title: Pair-combine divisibility sieve with free-frequency decoding (PS2)

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, the single algorithm PS2 of proof.md (pair-combine divisibility sieve, phase-estimation label extraction, free-frequency arc decoder, Shift-based 2-adic readout, with n = ceil(log2 N)) recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 2/3. In the challenge cost model this same algorithm and configuration has worst-case total work T(N,s) = O(2^(4 sqrt(n)) n^10) on every execution branch, hence the uniform bit-length envelope B_T(n) = 2^(4 sqrt(n)) n^10 with coefficient 4 on n^(1/2). All constants are absolute. The growth index of this envelope is exactly 1/2: log2 B_T = 4 n^(1/2) + 10 log2 n, so log2 log2 B_T = (1/2) log2 n + O(1). This holds jointly with the two workspace bounds and the sample bound below, and with the clean-input fractional tolerance epsilon(n) = 0.

For the same PS2 algorithm and configuration in proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, worst-case peak classical workspace is S_C(N,s) = O(2^(4 sqrt(n)) n^4) bits, with n = ceil(log2 N) and an absolute constant: the dominant term is the active sieve list of at most C0 = 2^(3q+b+8) labels in 2n-bit fields, with log2 C0 <= (5/sqrt 2) sqrt(n) + 12. Its envelope B_C(n) = 2^(4 sqrt(n)) n^4 has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the stated total-work bound, quantum-workspace bound and sample bound, and unconditional full-secret success probability at least 2/3.

For the same PS2 algorithm and configuration in proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, worst-case peak quantum workspace is S_Q(N,s) = O(2^(4 sqrt(n)) n^4) qubits, with n = ceil(log2 N) and an absolute constant: one active sieve run holds at most 2 C0 + K + O(n) live qubits, roots are measured immediately, and released registers are reused. Its envelope B_Q(n) = 2^(4 sqrt(n)) n^4 has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the stated total-work bound, classical-workspace bound and sample bound, and unconditional full-secret success probability at least 2/3.

For the same PS2 algorithm and configuration in proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, the total number Q(N,s) of fresh DCP source copies acquired is at most Qcap = 2^10 * 600 * n * C0(d0-1) on every execution branch, hence O(2^(4 sqrt(n)) n^7); this cap counts every discarded copy, failed sieve attempt and restarted decoder stage, and is enforced by a hard acquisition counter that stops and outputs 0 before exceeding it. The uniform bit-length envelope B_samples(n) = 2^(4 sqrt(n)) n^7 has growth index exactly 1/2. This bound holds jointly with the stated total-work and workspace bounds and unconditional full-secret success probability at least 2/3.

For the same PS2 algorithm and configuration in proof.md, the proved fractional error tolerance is epsilon(n)=0: all acquired copies are independent ideal coset states. Under this promise, for every N and s, full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 2/3 jointly with all four resource bounds above. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted; this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible. Each decoder root descends from 2^(q) = 2^(Theta(sqrt n)) source copies, so any positive adversarial malformed fraction that a sieve root must tolerate would first have to survive that ancestry; no such claim is made here.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
